scope_reason: Every structure that uses it is vanilla and in scope (SPEC Decisions: villages on, mineshafts, strongholds, temples and the Nether fortress vanilla).

notes: GPU-contract note: struct start holds a realloc-grown array of heap-allocated struct piece pointers (structure.c start_add), a pointer graph built during chunk population. The per-structure subclasses (MapGenVillage.Start, the stronghold Start, the fortress Start) are recorded with their own files. I did not open every evidence directory; the ones cited exist and test_structures/test_sblocks/test_populate read those trees per their headers. The disk half is n/a (lane/idxworld): every save this game makes is the oracle's (a checkpoint's save, session.sh's Save and Quit through Java: AGENTS.md 'Playing a full game'), and the native engine reads what it wrote (region.c for the overworld's region files, the snapshot's saved chunks for DIM-1 and DIM1, structures.json, villages.nbt, worldinfo.nbt, player_server.nbt); writing those files natively is the deferred product work of the 2026-09-25 triage (SPEC.md NEXT, '11 deferred save-writing'; out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md, 'Deferred, not noise'). Within a session nothing reads a save back: an unloaded chunk waits whole in the in-memory region store (sr_store_chunk) with what writeChunkToNBT keeps of it (the entities it saves, in section order; the pending ticks relative to the world time), and a reload restores exactly that (the persist-* and play-reload recordings).
